ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.summary: Refined sugar is a simple carbohydrate that provides calories without nutrients and can contribute to weight gain, blood sugar spikes, and increased risk of metabolic diseases when consumed in excess.

ingredients.name: Bleached wheat flour
ingredients.summary: Bleached wheat flour is refined grain flour treated with bleaching agents; it is lower in fiber and nutrients than whole grain and can rapidly raise blood sugar levels.

ingredients.name: Malted barley flour
ingredients.summary: Malted barley flour is a grain-based flour used to improve flavor and texture; it contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

ingredients.name: Niacin (vitamin B3)
ingredients.summary: Niacin is a B vitamin added for enrichment that supports energy metabolism and nervous system function; amounts in fortified foods are generally considered safe.

ingredients.name: Reduced iron
ingredients.summary: Reduced iron is an elemental iron powder used to fortify flour and prevent iron deficiency; typical fortification levels are considered safe for most people.

ingredients.name: Ferrous sulfate
ingredients.summary: Ferrous sulfate is an iron salt used for fortification to help prevent anemia; in normal food fortification doses it is generally safe, though high supplemental doses can cause gastrointestinal upset.

ingredients.name: Thiamine mononitrate (vitamin B1)
ingredients.summary: Thiamine mononitrate is a synthetic form of vitamin B1 used to enrich refined flour and supports energy metabolism and nerve function.

ingredients.name: Riboflavin (vitamin B2)
ingredients.summary: Riboflavin is vitamin B2 added for enrichment and is important for energy production and antioxidant functions; it is considered very safe at fortification levels.

ingredients.name: Folic acid (vitamin B9)
ingredients.summary: Folic acid is a synthetic form of folate used to fortify grains and help prevent neural tube defects; usual amounts in foods are considered safe for the general population.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.summary: Water is used as a basic solvent and moisture component in the product and poses no health concern in normal food use.

ingredients.name: High fructose corn syrup
ingredients.summary: High fructose corn syrup is a refined liquid sweetener high in fructose that is linked to increased risk of obesity, fatty liver, and metabolic syndrome when consumed frequently and in large amounts.

ingredients.name: Palm oil
ingredients.summary: Palm oil is a highly saturated vegetable fat that can raise LDL cholesterol when consumed in excess, though it is free of trans fats when not hydrogenated.

ingredients.name: Corn syrup
ingredients.summary: Corn syrup is a refined glucose-based sweetener that adds significant calories and can contribute to blood sugar spikes and weight gain when overconsumed.

ingredients.name: Cocoa
ingredients.summary: Cocoa is derived from cocoa beans and provides flavor and some beneficial polyphenols; in this context it is mainly used as a flavoring ingredient.

ingredients.name: Tallow
ingredients.summary: Tallow is rendered animal fat high in saturated fat, which can raise LDL cholesterol and is associated with increased cardiovascular risk when eaten frequently in large amounts.

ingredients.name: Soybean oil
ingredients.summary: Soybean oil is a common vegetable oil high in omega-6 fatty acids; excessive intake relative to omega-3s may promote inflammation, and it is also a potential allergen source for people with soy allergy.

ingredients.name: Glycerin
ingredients.summary: Glycerin is a humectant and sweet-tasting liquid used to retain moisture and improve texture; it is generally recognized as safe when consumed in normal food amounts.

ingredients.name: Cocoa processed with alkali
ingredients.summary: Cocoa processed with alkali (Dutch-processed cocoa) is cocoa treated to reduce acidity and create a milder flavor; it is safe for most people but may contain small amounts of caffeine and theobromine.

ingredients.name: Modified food starch
ingredients.summary: Modified food starch is starch that has been physically or chemically altered to improve thickening and stability; it is generally safe, though it can be a hidden source of gluten if not specified as gluten-free.

ingredients.name: Corn starch
ingredients.summary: Corn starch is a refined carbohydrate used as a thickener and texturizer; it is generally safe but offers little nutritional value and can raise blood sugar when consumed in large amounts.

ingredients.name: Baking soda
ingredients.summary: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) is a leavening agent that helps baked goods rise; it is safe in normal food quantities but contributes a small amount of sodium.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.summary: Salt (sodium chloride) is used for flavor and preservation; high intake is linked to elevated blood pressure and cardiovascular risk, so overall dietary sodium load is the main concern.

ingredients.name: Whey
ingredients.summary: Whey is a milk-derived protein used for texture and protein content; it is a common allergen for people with dairy allergy or severe lactose intolerance.

ingredients.name: Corn syrup solids
ingredients.summary: Corn syrup solids are dehydrated corn syrup used as a sweetener and bulking agent; they are a concentrated source of simple sugars that can contribute to blood sugar spikes and excess calorie intake.

ingredients.name: Calcium sulfate
ingredients.summary: Calcium sulfate is a mineral salt used as a firming agent and dough conditioner; it is generally recognized as safe and also provides a small amount of calcium.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.summary: Egg is used for structure and richness in foods; it is a major allergen and can cause serious reactions in people with egg allergy.

ingredients.name: Agave syrup
ingredients.summary: Agave syrup is a liquid sweetener high in fructose; while it has a lower immediate impact on blood glucose than some sugars, high fructose intake is associated with potential metabolic and liver concerns when consumed in excess.

ingredients.name: Inulin
ingredients.summary: Inulin is a soluble dietary fiber and prebiotic used to improve texture and fiber content; it is generally beneficial but may cause gas or bloating in sensitive individuals or in large amounts.

ingredients.name: Egg whites
ingredients.summary: Egg whites provide protein and structure; they are still part of the egg allergen group and can trigger reactions in people allergic to eggs.

ingredients.name: Dextrose
ingredients.summary: Dextrose is a simple sugar (glucose) used as a sweetener and to aid browning; it rapidly raises blood sugar and can contribute to excess calorie intake when heavily consumed.

ingredients.name: Hydrogenated tallow
ingredients.summary: Hydrogenated tallow is animal fat that has been hydrogenated, a process that can create trans fats; trans fats are strongly linked to increased LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular disease risk.

ingredients.name: Sodium acid pyrophosphate
ingredients.summary: Sodium acid pyrophosphate is a leavening acid and sequestrant that helps baked goods rise and maintain color; it adds to overall sodium and phosphate intake, which may be a concern for people with kidney disease or on sodium-restricted diets.

ingredients.name: Mono- and diglycerides
ingredients.summary: Emulsifiers derived from fats that help blend oil and water; generally recognized as safe but may contain small amounts of trans fats depending on source and processing.

ingredients.name: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate)
ingredients.summary: A common leavening agent used to help baked goods rise; considered safe at typical food-use levels.

ingredients.name: Polysorbate 60
ingredients.summary: A synthetic emulsifier used to improve texture and shelf life; approved for use but some studies raise questions about potential effects on gut barrier and microbiome at high or chronic intakes.

ingredients.name: Sodium stearoyl lactylate
ingredients.summary: An emulsifier used in baked goods to improve dough strength and texture; generally recognized as safe, though it is a marker of processed foods.

ingredients.name: Cottonseed oil
ingredients.summary: A refined vegetable oil often high in omega-6 fats and sometimes from genetically modified crops; highly processed oils may contribute to an imbalanced fatty acid intake when consumed frequently.

ingredients.name: Soy lecithin
ingredients.summary: A soy-derived emulsifier that helps ingredients mix smoothly; generally safe but may be a concern for people with soy allergy or strict soy avoidance.

ingredients.name: Xanthan gum
ingredients.summary: A thickener and stabilizer produced by fermentation; usually well tolerated, though large amounts may cause digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Agar
ingredients.summary: A gelling agent derived from seaweed used to thicken or gel foods; generally safe and a source of soluble fiber.

ingredients.name: Cellulose gum (carboxymethyl cellulose)
ingredients.summary: A synthetic form of plant fiber used as a thickener and stabilizer; considered safe, but some research suggests certain emulsifiers and gums may affect gut barrier function in high or chronic intake.

ingredients.name: Natural and artificial flavors
ingredients.summary: A mixture of flavoring chemicals, some from natural sources and some synthetic; composition is not disclosed, which limits transparency and may be an issue for sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Color (artificial or unspecified coloring agents)
ingredients.summary: Added coloring agents to enhance appearance; risk depends on specific dyes used, and some artificial colors have been linked to hyperactivity or sensitivity in susceptible individuals.

ingredients.name: Monocalcium phosphate
ingredients.summary: A leavening acid used in baking powders to help dough rise; generally recognized as safe at typical food-use levels.

ingredients.name: Enzymes
ingredients.summary: Processing aids that modify dough or texture; typically present in very small amounts, though the exact source is often not disclosed (which may matter for some allergen or dietary concerns).

ingredients.name: Salt (sodium chloride)
ingredients.summary: Common seasoning and preservative; safe in small amounts, but high overall dietary sodium intake is associated with increased blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.

ingredients.name: Locust bean gum (carob bean gum)
ingredients.summary: A plant-derived thickener and stabilizer from carob tree seeds; generally well tolerated and widely used in foods.

ingredients.name: Dipotassium phosphate
ingredients.summary: A buffering and stabilizing salt that can also act as a mineral supplement; usually safe, but excessive intake of phosphate additives may be a concern for people with kidney disease or those consuming many processed foods.

ingredients.name: Chocolate liquor
ingredients.summary: Chocolate liquor is the ground, roasted cocoa mass (non‑alcoholic) that provides cocoa solids and cocoa butter; it is generally safe for most people but contains caffeine and theobromine, which may be an issue in large amounts or for sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Defatted soy flour
ingredients.summary: Defatted soy flour is made from soybeans with most of the oil removed and is high in protein; it is a common allergen and contains soy isoflavones, which may affect hormone-sensitive individuals, so it is flagged mainly for allergenicity.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.summary: Milk provides protein, lactose, and milk fats but is a major allergen; it can trigger reactions in people with milk allergy and digestive issues in those with lactose intolerance.

ingredients.name: Soybean
ingredients.summary: Soybean is a legume used widely as a protein source and processing ingredient; it is a common allergen and may cause reactions ranging from mild to severe in sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Wheat
ingredients.summary: Wheat is a cereal grain that commonly contains gluten; it is a major allergen and can cause serious issues for people with celiac disease, non‑celiac gluten sensitivity, or wheat allergy.

ingredients.name: Bioengineered food ingredients (GMOs)
ingredients.summary: Bioengineered food ingredients (genetically modified organisms, GMOs) are crops or components altered using biotechnology; current evidence does not show clear harm in humans, but they are flagged due to ongoing debate, environmental concerns, and the possibility of increased pesticide exposure depending on the crop.

ingredients.name: Palm oil
ingredients.summary: A common vegetable oil high in saturated fat; frequent intake, especially in highly processed foods, is associated with less favorable heart-health profiles.

ingredients.name: Canola oil
ingredients.summary: A vegetable oil relatively low in saturated fat and commonly used for cooking and in processed foods.

ingredients.name: Soy lecithin
ingredients.summary: An emulsifier derived from soy that helps blend fats and water; generally recognized as safe but derived from a major allergen (soy).

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.summary: Refined or possibly enriched wheat flour provides carbohydrates but little fiber; it contains gluten, which is problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.summary: Refined sugar contributes to excess calorie intake, blood sugar spikes, and increased risk of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dental caries when consumed in large amounts.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.summary: Common table salt (sodium chloride); high intake is linked to elevated blood pressure and cardiovascular risk, especially in processed foods.

ingredients.name: Corn starch
ingredients.summary: A refined starch used as a thickener or texturizer; mainly a source of rapidly digested carbohydrate.

ingredients.name: Spices
ingredients.summary: A mixture of dried plant seasonings; generally beneficial or neutral, though specific spice sensitivities are possible in some individuals.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.summary: A culinary herb used for flavor; may have cardiovascular and antimicrobial benefits, though some people experience digestive sensitivity.

ingredients.name: Whole milk powder
ingredients.summary: Dehydrated whole milk containing lactose and milk proteins; a source of saturated fat and a major allergen for those with dairy allergy or lactose intolerance.

ingredients.name: Skim milk powder
ingredients.summary: Dehydrated nonfat milk that still contains lactose and milk proteins; lower in fat but remains a common allergen.

ingredients.name: Caramel color
ingredients.summary: A brown food color made by heating sugars; some types can contain trace levels of 4-MEI, which has raised cancer-related concerns in high exposures.

ingredients.name: Monosodium glutamate
ingredients.summary: A flavor enhancer providing umami taste; considered safe for most people, though some report sensitivity symptoms such as headaches or flushing.

ingredients.name: Defatted soybean
ingredients.summary: Soybeans with most of the fat removed, used as a protein source; nutritionally dense but a major allergen for those with soy allergy.

ingredients.name: Yeast extract
ingredients.summary: A flavoring rich in glutamates that enhances savory taste; safe for most but can be an issue for those sensitive to glutamate-rich ingredients.

ingredients.name: Natural and artificial flavors
ingredients.summary: A blend of unspecified flavoring chemicals; generally recognized as safe but poorly transparent, which can be problematic for people with specific sensitivities.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.summary: A natural sweetener containing sugars and trace bioactive compounds; still contributes to overall sugar load and should be moderated.

ingredients.name: Dextrin
ingredients.summary: A group of short-chain carbohydrates derived from starch, used as a filler or thickener; rapidly digested and can raise blood glucose.

ingredients.name: Pasteurized milk
ingredients.summary: Heat-treated milk to kill pathogens; nutritionally useful but a common allergen and source of lactose.

ingredients.name: Cheese cultures
ingredients.summary: Beneficial bacteria used to ferment milk into cheese; generally safe and may support gut health.

ingredients.name: Enzymes
ingredients.summary: Processing aids used to modify texture or flavor (such as rennet or other food enzymes); typically present in very small amounts and considered safe.

ingredients.name: Onion flake
ingredients.summary: Dehydrated pieces of onion used for flavor; generally safe, though some individuals may have onion sensitivity.

ingredients.name: Natural flavor
ingredients.summary: A broad term for flavoring substances derived from natural sources; safety is generally acceptable but composition is not transparent for people with sensitivities.

ingredients.name: Onion extract
ingredients.summary: Concentrated onion-derived flavoring; safe for most but may trigger symptoms in those sensitive to alliums.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce (soybean, wheat, salt)
ingredients.summary: A fermented seasoning made from soybeans, wheat, and salt; high in sodium and contains both soy and gluten allergens.

ingredients.name: Garlic extract
ingredients.summary: Concentrated garlic-derived flavoring; generally safe but can cause digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Tomato powder
ingredients.summary: Dehydrated tomato used for flavor and color; provides some antioxidants like lycopene.

ingredients.name: Dried onion
ingredients.summary: Dehydrated onion pieces used as a seasoning; safe for most but may affect those with onion intolerance.

ingredients.name: Glucose
ingredients.summary: A simple sugar that rapidly raises blood sugar levels; frequent intake in processed foods can contribute to metabolic issues.

ingredients.name: Sucrose fatty acid esters
ingredients.summary: Emulsifiers made from sucrose and fatty acids used to stabilize mixtures; considered safe at typical intakes but are markers of ultra-processed foods.

ingredients.name: Dextrose anhydrous (glucose)
ingredients.summary: A dry form of pure glucose used as a sweetener or carrier; quickly absorbed and can spike blood sugar.

ingredients.name: Banana
ingredients.summary: A fruit ingredient providing natural sugars, potassium, and fiber (though some fiber may be reduced in processed form).

ingredients.name: Processed honey
ingredients.summary: Honey that has been heated or filtered; still primarily sugar and contributes to overall added sugar intake.

ingredients.name: Tomato paste
ingredients.summary: Concentrated tomato product used for flavor and color; a source of lycopene and other phytonutrients.

ingredients.name: Fermented milk
ingredients.summary: Milk that has been cultured with bacteria (similar to yogurt or kefir); may aid digestion but remains a dairy allergen.

ingredients.name: Citric acid
ingredients.summary: A common acidity regulator and preservative often produced by fermentation; generally safe, though it may irritate mouth sores in sensitive people.

ingredients.name: Mono- and diglycerides
ingredients.summary: Emulsifiers derived from glycerol and fatty acids; can contain small amounts of trans fats and are typical of ultra-processed foods.

ingredients.name: Alkali (alkalizing agents)
ingredients.summary: Alkali refers to alkaline substances (such as sodium or potassium carbonates) used to adjust acidity; in typical food-use amounts they are generally recognized as safe but contribute to overall sodium or mineral load.

ingredients.name: Tomato extract
ingredients.summary: Tomato extract is a concentrated form of tomato used for flavor and color, providing natural pigments and some antioxidants like lycopene.

ingredients.name: Salt (sodium chloride)
ingredients.summary: Salt is used for flavor and preservation; high intake is linked to elevated blood pressure and cardiovascular risk, so frequent consumption of salty processed foods is a concern.

ingredients.name: Soy protein hydrolysate
ingredients.summary: Soy protein hydrolysate is enzymatically broken-down soy protein used as a flavor enhancer and protein source; it is an allergen for people with soy allergy and may contain free glutamates similar to MSG.

ingredients.name: Apple puree
ingredients.summary: Apple puree is a mashed apple product used for flavor and mild sweetness, providing some natural sugars and small amounts of fiber and phytonutrients.

ingredients.name: Dried garlic
ingredients.summary: Dried garlic is dehydrated garlic used for flavor and may provide some beneficial sulfur compounds; it is safe for most people except those with garlic sensitivity.

ingredients.name: Maltose
ingredients.summary: Maltose is a disaccharide sugar derived from starch, used as a sweetener; like other added sugars, high intake can contribute to blood sugar spikes and metabolic problems.

ingredients.name: Whey powder
ingredients.summary: Whey powder is a dairy-derived protein and lactose source; it is a milk allergen and can cause issues for people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

ingredients.name: Garlic flake
ingredients.summary: Garlic flakes are dried pieces of garlic used for flavor; they are generally safe and may offer some of garlic’s beneficial compounds.

ingredients.name: Paprika color
ingredients.summary: Paprika color is a natural pigment extracted from paprika peppers, used for red-orange color and mild flavor; it is typically safe and not associated with the concerns of synthetic dyes.

ingredients.name: Disodium inosinate
ingredients.summary: Disodium inosinate is a flavor enhancer often used with MSG to intensify savory taste; it is generally safe at low levels but may be a concern for individuals sensitive to flavor enhancers.

ingredients.name: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
ingredients.summary: Monosodium glutamate is a widely used flavor enhancer that boosts umami taste; it is considered safe for most people, but some individuals report sensitivity symptoms such as headaches or flushing.
